title: A portal's glass shows its destination through a window that parallaxes with the viewer's eye, and a pick through it lands on the destination's surface
binding: The positive leg boots an offscreen 256x144 world whose one placement, a door, has a glass face carrying a portal facet (destination 'beyond', arrival mapped onto the destination's 'arch/glass' counterpart) and showing a session of that same destination with the window projection. The destination (beyond.world.json) is a persisted global world holding an arch at the door's position facing it, a green emissive marker of radius one half six units behind the arch, a blue emissive backdrop twelve units behind it, and a magenta emissive slab four units in front of the arch, between the window's mapped eye and the arch's glass, wide enough to fill the window from either eye. A fixed camera looks at the door from six units back, and the seat's body stands nine units back, behind the camera, so its eye fits the window without entering the frame. world.screens lists the glass as screen 24 showing session:beyond, bound, its mapping naming the session instance over the glass (0.96x0.8 half extents, proud of the face at z 0.1) at the session's 144x120 extent, with no bezel warp. The body steps a unit right of the door and the captured frame shows the marker right of the glass's centre against the blue backdrop, with the glass left of centre blue; it steps a unit left and the marker shows left of centre, with the glass right of centre blue, so the window reframes the destination from the viewer's eye. The session publishes its float working image, so the marker's emissive headroom reaches the glass unclamped and only the frame's one display encode clips it: the marker reads green-dominant (green at least 0.45, red at most 0.25, blue at most 0.5), where the blue backdrop's green is at most 0.3. The window's camera starts every ray on the glass, so the slab before the aperture never shows: nowhere on the glass does red exceed 0.3, which the magenta slab's would. With the view at three-quarter scale, a display point on the marker's image walks through the room's view onto the glass (session$24's pixel 43,58), through the camera the window rendered into the destination's world, and lands on the marker's near surface at 0.02,1.47,-5.5, passing the slab; a point beside it lands on the backdrop at 1.4,1.42,-11.9. The discriminating leg shows a window onto a different destination (elsewhere.world.json: the same arch before a red backdrop, with no marker and the same magenta emissive material on a ball of radius one half five and a half units behind the arch, beyond the aperture): the screen lists session:elsewhere, both marker observations and both blue observations fail, the ball shows magenta where the marker showed, so magenta beyond the aperture reaches the glass (red and blue at least 0.5, since the ball's shaded limb falls below the marker's floor), and the pick on the marker's image lands on the ball instead, while the pick beside it lands on the backdrop at 1.39,1.42,-11.9, the positive leg's point to within the march's hit band: the ball beside that ray shortens the march's steps, so it stops at another point of the same band, which the two-decimal print rounds the other way. That the walk reaches the same backdrop pixel shows it runs the same way through either window.

expect.text: 24 session:beyond bound fixed input:Presentation mapping instance:session$24 surface origin 0,1.5,0.1 right 1,0,0 up 0,1,0 half 0.96x0.8 source 144x120 crop 0,0 144x120 layout Identity fit Stretch destination Presentation
